title: FLA import: scale9Grid not decoded — 9-slice scaling lost on round-trip
description:
The symbol model supports scale9Grid (a { left, top, right, bottom } rectangle) and compile.ts emits DefineScalingGrid (tag 78) correctly. However flash8-binary.ts has no code to read it from the FLA binary stream, and flash8-import.ts always leaves scale9Grid as null for imported symbols.

In Flash 8 binary FLAs, the 9-slice grid rectangle is stored in the Symbol N CPicPage afterData (after the CPicPage children list and registration point). The flacomdoc FlaConverter encodes it; the exact byte layout needs to be verified against flacomdoc writeFlashMovieInfo or the symbol-level afterData block.

Steps:
1. Locate the scale9Grid encoding in flacomdoc FlaConverter (likely in writeSymbol or writeFlashMovieInfo — look for '9slice', 'Scale9', or 'splitter' references)
2. Add a scale9Grid field to Fla8Timeline (or Fla8ContentsInfo via the symbol table)
3. Decode it in flash8-binary.ts (parseFla8Timeline or CPicPage afterData reader)
4. Wire it through flash8-import.ts to createSymbol() options

Without this, any imported FLA that uses 9-slice scaling (common for UI panels and buttons) will scale uniformly and distort corners in Ruffle.
